# Checking out an older .sesam and sealing on top of it forks the audit log:
# the next commit would drop entries HEAD already holds. Committed history alone
# looks fine until that commit lands, so the hook compares the staged log too.

sesam-repo admin a.txt b.txt c.txt d.txt
exec sesam hook install

cp $TMPDIR/a.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'one'
cp $TMPDIR/b.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'two'
cp $TMPDIR/c.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'three'

exec git checkout HEAD^^ -- .sesam
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A

# verify sees it before the commit, naming the staged changes.
! exec sesam verify --all
stderr 'is not a prefix of the staged changes'
stderr 'audit log may only grow'
stderr 'git checkout <rev> -- .sesam'
stderr 'git checkout HEAD -- .:/.sesam. && sesam seal'

# The hook refuses the commit.
! exec git commit -m 'oops'
stderr 'is not a prefix of the staged changes'
stderr 'verification failed'
exec git log --oneline
! stdout 'oops'

# The suggested way out: take .sesam from HEAD and seal again.
exec git checkout HEAD -- ':/.sesam'
cp $TMPDIR/d.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'redo'
exec sesam verify --all

-- a.txt --
A
-- b.txt --
B
-- c.txt --
C
-- d.txt --
D
